Patrick Wahome, who has organised protests in Nanyuki against the centre, told Reuters on Tuesday the man died from a gunshot wound to the head. Reporters from the agency saw his body lying motionless in a police van with a large head wound.

A former Air Canada pilot has been charged after flying for years without a proper license, Canadian police have said.

Geoffrey Wall, of Barrie, Ontario, is alleged to have operated as an airline captain between 2009 and 2025 without a license to fly large commercial passenger planes, according to Peel regional police.

About 20,000 people have signed a petition on Change.org entitled Protect Japanese Manga, protesting against the official White House X account posting videos featuring unauthorised use of imagery from the popular Dragon Ball, Yu-Gi-Oh! and Naruto series.

At least 37 people have died and hundreds have been injured after a magnitude-7.8 earthquake shook part of the southern Philippines early on Monday, collapsing buildings and triggering tsunami alerts.

Xi Jinping has arrived in North Korea for a two-day trip, his first in nearly seven years, as China’s leader looks to revitalise ties with his junior ally.

Footage published by China’s Xinhua state news agency showed an Air China plane carrying Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, touching down at Pyongyang’s Sunan international airport.

rfi.title: Children in danger 'not heard' in France, rights lawyer warns after Lyhanna death
rfi.description: The abduction and killing of 11-year-old French schoolgirl Lyhanna has catapaulted child protection to the top of France's political agenda – with President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday calling for full accountability and the government pledging full transparency. As investigators examine possible failures by the justice system, child rights lawyer Dominique Attias tells RFI professionals have been warning for years that vulnerable children are not being protected.

rfi.title: Amnesty accuses Israel of ‘ethnic cleansing’ of West Bank Bedouin communities
rfi.description: Amnesty International has accused Israel of carrying out what it described as a state-led campaign of “ethnic cleansing” against Bedouin and herding communities in the occupied West Bank, saying the measures were intended to accelerate the annexation of Palestinian territory.

rfi.title: Europe faces growing threat from synthetic opioids and new drugs, report warns
rfi.description: Highly potent synthetic opioids are spreading through Europe's fast-changing drug market, linked to hundreds of deaths as traffickers shift to smaller ports and new smuggling methods, the European Union Drugs Agency (EUDA) has warned.

rfi.title: European heatwave drives world's second-hottest May on record
rfi.description: The world experienced its second-hottest May on record in 2026 as an unusually early and intense heatwave swept across Europe, setting new temperature records across the continent, the European Union's Copernicus Climate Change Service said on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Pope Leo to celebrate mass at Barcelona's unfinished Sagrada Familia
rfi.description: Pope Leo XIV will celebrate mass at Barcelona's Sagrada Família on Wednesday and bless its final tower, marking the completion of Antoni Gaudí's masterpiece and making it the tallest church in the world. The pontiff arrived in Spain at the weekend for a week-long visit focused on immigration and politics.

rfi.title: Kenyan protester killed at demonstration against US Ebola facility
rfi.description: Kenyan police shot dead a protester on Tuesday as hundreds demonstrated against a government-backed quarantine centre for Americans exposed to Ebola, with anger mounting over Nairobi's determination to press ahead with the facility.

rfi.title: Belfast unrest erupts after stabbing linked to Sudanese refugee
rfi.description: Belfast anti-immigration protesters set vehicles and buildings on fire on Tuesday night, a day after a knife attack allegedly carried out by a Sudanese refugee seriously injured a man and was captured in a graphic video that spread widely online.

rfi.title: Africa's finest: Ghana to seek World Cup redemption under new coach Queiroz
rfi.description: Ghana enter the first 48-team World Cup ranked 14th among African sides in the Fifa standings. In the final instalment of a nine-part series on African squads at the 2026 tournament, hosted across the United States, Mexico and Canada, RFI looks at a nation making its fifth World Cup appearance.

rfi.title: French PM announces measures to combat child abuse amid Lyhanna protests
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Tuesday presented initial measures to better protect children, following a meeting with key ministers, in a bid to quell public anger sweeping the country over the death of 11-year-old Lyhanna.

rfi.title: Oxfam warns Europe’s corporate giants are fuelling inequality
rfi.description: Europe’s biggest companies are paying more than two-thirds of their profits to shareholders on average, diverting money that could otherwise support investment, climate action and workers’ wages, according to Oxfam.

rfi.title: France moves closer to ocean goals with three new marine protection zones
rfi.description: The French government has announced three new marine protected areas, bringing it a step closer to goals established at the 2025 United Nations Ocean Summit. These "strong protection" zones are situated in mainland France, in the French West Indies and the French Southern and Antarctic Lands.

rfi.title: Africa's sound, African film at Cannes and the World Cup kick-off
rfi.description: This week, Spotlight on Africa explores cinema and music scoring for African documentary projects with storytellers from Mozambique and Kenya. We will also bring you news from the Cannes Film Festival, along with the African teams selected to take part in the football World Cup.

rfi.title: Platini sues Infantino in French courts as Fifa feud heats up
rfi.description: Former Uefa president Michel Platini said on Monday he is suing Fifa president Gianni Infantino, in the latest chapter of a battle that began when scandal derailed Platini's 2015 bid for the Fifa presidency. After unsuccessful attempts in Switzerland, Platini is now turning to the French justice system to make his case.

rfi.title: Somali football referee denied US entry will miss World Cup debut
rfi.description: The United States has denied entry to football referee Omar Abdulkadir Artan, who had been expected to be the first Somali to officiate a World Cup match.

rfi.title: French star Wembanyama leads Spurs fightback against Knicks
rfi.description: French basketball star Victor Wembanyama scored 32 points as the San Antonio Spurs beat the New York Knicks 115-111 to relaunch their bid for the 2026 NBA crown.

rfi.title: Merz and Macron agree to scrap FCAS joint fighter jet programme
rfi.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron have agreed to abandon a joint fighter jet programme due to long-running disagreements between the companies involved, the German government said on Monday.

rfi.title: French NATO jets destroy mystery drone over Latvia as Ukraine war intensifies
rfi.description: French NATO fighter jets stationed in the Baltic region shot down a drone that had entered Latvian airspace on Monday, marking a rare interception under the alliance’s Baltic Air Policing mission. It follows a series of similar incidents linked to the war in Ukraine as Moscow and Kyiv step up drone strikes on each other.

rfi.title: EU says Ebola outbreak makes ceasefire in DRC more necessary than ever
rfi.description: The European Union’s crisis management commissioner has called for a ceasefire between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda, saying the need for peace has become even more urgent with the spread of the Ebola outbreak.

euronews.description: The new US assault across multiple Iranian cities came as efforts to negotiate an end the war again appeared stuck, with Iran insisting it would maintain its chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz, which has disrupted global energy supplies and sent oil prices higher.

euronews.description: Bulgaria, which is member of NATO and the European Union, has been providing military aid Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.

euronews.description: The Agriculture and Food Commissioner warned that, to avoid looming food shortages in the face of rising fertiliser costs, the bloc must secure sustainable fertiliser supplies and not just provide short-term financial support.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : les Etats-Unis poursuivent leurs frappes sur l’Iran, les gardiens de la révolution disent avoir mené des tirs de riposte au Koweït, à Bahreïn et en Jordanie
lemonde.description: Le commandement militaire américain pour le Moyen-Orient dit avoir visé « des installations de surveillance militaire, des systèmes de communication et des sites de défense aérienne ». L’armée américaine avait démenti plus tôt les affirmations de Téhéran selon lesquelles il aurait fermé le détroit d’Ormuz.

lemonde.title: Patrick Bruel mis en examen pour viol, tentative de viol, agression sexuelle et harcèlement sexuel, et placé sous contrôle judiciaire
lemonde.description: Le chanteur est mis en examen pour quatre affaires et placé sous le statut de témoin assisté dans quatre autres dossiers, a précisé l’une de ses avocates. Le juge des libertés et de la détention du tribunal de Nanterre n’a pas suivi les réquisitions du parquet qui avait demandé un placement en détention provisoire.

lemonde.title: Le réchauffement climatique dû aux activités humaines devrait atteindre 1,5 °C autour de 2030
lemonde.description: Dans une étude publiée le 11 juin, un consortium de chercheurs confirme que le seuil le plus ambitieux de l’accord de Paris sur le climat, signé en 2015, devrait être dépassé dans les quatre prochaines années.

lemonde.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : avant le coup d’envoi, Gianni Infantino slalome entre les polémiques
lemonde.description: A la veille du match d’ouverture du Mondial, opposant le Mexique à l’Afrique du Sud jeudi à Mexico, le président décrié de la Fédération internationale de football a balayé les sujets qui fâchent, lors de sa conférence de presse.

lemonde.title: Bac de français : les enseignants face au défi croissant de donner le goût de la lecture et de la littérature aux élèves
lemonde.description: Alors que les élèves planchent, jeudi 11 juin, sur l’épreuve anticipée de français, des professeurs de lettres déplorent que le formalisme des exercices demandés ainsi que la liste des œuvres classiques étudiées ne favorisent pas l’envie de lire, en crise, au sein de leurs classes.

lemonde.title: Belfast : nouvelle nuit de violences, la police utilise un canon à eau pour disperser les manifestants
lemonde.description: Des émeutes anti-immigrés avaient déjà eu lieu dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi dans la capitale nord-irlandaise, à la suite d’une attaque au couteau, lundi soir. D’importantes forces policières ont été déployées.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, affaire Lyhanna : les obsèques de la fillette se dérouleront vendredi « dans la plus stricte intimité »
lemonde.description: Emmanuel Macron a reconnu mercredi que la question de « la confiance dans nos institutions » était posée, tout en mettant en garde contre toute « démagogie » et « précipitation » à légiférer.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Volodymyr Zelensky participera au sommet du G7 mardi, annonce Emmanuel Macron
lemonde.description: « C’est très important pour nous parce qu’il faut recréer de la convergence au G7, en soutien à l’Ukraine », y compris sur la nécessité de négociations, a déclaré le président français, dans une allusion aux divergences entre les Européens et Donald Trump sur ce dossier.

lemonde.title: La France sans nouveau budget jusqu’à la présidentielle en 2027 : le scénario qui divise
lemonde.description: Les députés socialistes viennent de boucler une proposition de loi pour permettre à la France de tenir des mois si aucun budget ne peut être adopté. Le gouvernement, lui, ne veut pas entendre parler d’une nouvelle loi spéciale.

lemonde.title: Droits de douane : le Trésor américain a remboursé 22 milliards de dollars en mai
lemonde.description: En février, la Cour suprême avait annulé les surtaxes portant sur l’ensemble des produits entrant aux Etats-Unis, estimant que Donald Trump avait, en les imposant, outrepassé les pouvoirs que lui conférait la Constitution américaine.

lemonde.title: Une ONG accuse l’Europe de fermer les yeux sur les importations provenant des colonies israéliennes
lemonde.description: S’appuyant sur 30 000 bordereaux d’exportation collectés pendant quatre ans, l’ONG Global Echo Litigation Center révèle une fraude systématique sur l’origine des produits agricoles issus des colonies en Cisjordanie occupée et dénonce la complicité de l’Europe.

lemonde.title: Le Canada veut interdire à son tour les réseaux sociaux aux moins de 16 ans
lemonde.description: Dans le sillage d’autres pays ayant déjà mis en place des interdictions, comme l’Australie, le gouvernement canadien met en avant les effets nocifs sur la santé mentale des mineurs des réseaux sociaux, « source d’anxiété, d’isolement, de dépression ».

lemonde.title: Notre sélection de livres cette semaine : « A Palmares », « Cautère », « Latéral gauche »…
lemonde.description: Chaque jeudi, la rédaction du « Monde des livres » vous propose ses choix littéraires. Aujourd’hui, notamment, un roman de Gayl Jones rappelant les mythes grecs, acclamé aux Etats-Unis.

lemonde.title: A Barcelone, Léon XIV voit dans la basilique de la Sagrada Familia un « phare » pour l’évangélisation
lemonde.description: En visite dans la capitale de la Catalogne, la région d’Espagne la plus sécularisée, le pape a commémoré le centenaire de la mort du concepteur de l’édifice, Antoni Gaudi, surnommé « l’architecte de Dieu ».

lemonde.title: Un jeune couple de pandas roux chinois « infiltré » à Taïwan
lemonde.description: En provenance de Shanghaï, un mâle de 3 ans et une femelle de 2 ans sont arrivés au zoo de Taipei en échange de deux gibbons. Une première depuis 2014, et un cadeau pas vraiment innocent dans le contexte actuel extrêmement tendu entre les deux rives du détroit de Formose.

lemonde.title: Donald Trump dit « aimer » l’inflation, pourtant galopante aux Etats-Unis
lemonde.description: Les prix ont augmenté, en mai, de 4,2 % sur un an, contre 3,8 % en avril –, une très forte accélération à quelques mois des élections de mi-mandat.

france24fr.title: Finale NBA : les Spurs de Wembanyama s'effondrent chez les Knicks, qui mènent 3-1
france24fr.description: Les New York Knicks ne sont plus qu'à une victoire du titre NBA, après leur folle remontée face aux San Antonio Spurs mercredi soir lors du match 4 de la finale. Flamboyant en début de partie, le Français Victor Wembanyama s'est effondré à l'image du collectif texan.

france24fr.title: En direct : l'Iran, à nouveau bombardé par les États-Unis, promet de refermer le détroit d'Ormuz
En direct : l'Iran, à nouveau bombardé par les États-Unis, promet de refermer le détroit d'Ormuz
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis ont mené jeudi à l'aube de nouveaux bombardements contre l'Iran, qui a annoncé des ripostes contre des bases militaires au Koweït et à Bahreïn et promis de prendre pour cible tous les navires s'aventurant dans le détroit d'Ormuz. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Gianni Infantino espère une grâce de l'Algérie pour Christophe Gleizes
france24fr.description: Le patron de la Fifa Gianni Infantino a donné une conférence de presse mercredi à Mexico, à la veille du match d'ouverture du Mondial 2026. Il a notamment dit espérer que le président algérien accorde une grâce au journaliste sportif français Christophe Gleizes afin qu'il puisse venir couvrir le tournoi pour lequel il a reçu une accréditation.

france24fr.title: Les plus gros scandales de la Coupe du monde
france24fr.description: C'est ce jeudi que débute la Coupe du monde de football et avant même qu'elle n'est commencée, cette 23ème édition est marquée par plusieurs polémiques. Mais c'est un peu le lot de chaque édition depuis 1930.

france24fr.title: En direct : l'armée américaine dit mener des "frappes défensives" contre l'Iran
Mondial 2026 : les Bleus sont arrivés à leur camp de base de Boston
france24fr.description: Les joueurs de l'équipe de France de football sont arrivés mardi à Boston où est établi leur camp de base pour le Mondial 2026. Ils affronteront le Sénégal le 16 juin : les Bleus ont donc six jours pour se faire au décalage horaire et s'acclimater à la chaleur de la côte Est américaine.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : l'équipe du Sénégal "humiliée" par les douanes à leur arrivée aux États-Unis ?
france24fr.description: A la veille de la Coupe du Monde de football 2026, une vidéo montre l'équipe du Sénégal en pleine fouille sur un tarmac. Plusieurs utilisateurs y voient une "humiliation raciste" à leur entrée sur le territoire américain. Ces images, véridiques, montrent en réalité un contrôle de routine pour les vols privés. La fédération de football sénégalaise a confirmé que cette procédure, opérée "sans incident", avait été organisée pour permettre aux joueurs d'éviter les files d'attente dans l'aérogare.

france24fr.title: Retour d’Omar Artan en héros à Mogadiscio : "Je serai là à la prochaine Coupe du monde" en 2030
france24fr.description: Omar Artane, l’arbitre somalien refoulé des États-Unis, est rentré chez lui. Il est arrivé en Somalie ce mercredi. Il a été accueilli en héros, en présence de plusieurs membres du gouvernement. Il a promis à ses soutiens qu’il participerait à la Coupe du monde 2030.

france24fr.title: Patrick Bruel mis en examen pour viol, tentative de viol, agression sexuelle et harcèlement sexuel
J-2 avant l'entrée en Bourse de SpaceX
france24fr.description: À l'occasion de son entrée en Bourse prévue le 12 juin, SpaceX espère lever 75 milliards de dollars et atteindre une valorisation de près de 1 800 milliards de dollars, ce qui en ferait l'introduction boursière la plus importante de l'histoire. L'opération est très attendue par les investisseurs, mais également redoutée par certains en raison du manque de rentabilité de la compagnie d'Elon Musk.

france24fr.title: Bilan carbone: le Mondial 2026 sera le plus émetteur de gaz à effet de serre de l'Histoire
france24fr.description: Selon le dossier de candidature, le Mondial 2026 devait être le moins polluant de l'Histoire. Il pourrait être, à l'inverse, le plus émetteur de gaz à effet de serre. La faute aux nombreux kilomètres avalés en avion entre des stades répartis sur tout le continent nord-américain. La faute aussi au nombre record d'équipes participantes (porté de 32 à 48). +92% d'émissions pour cette édition par rapport à la moyenne des décennies précédentes selon l'association SGR.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la vidéo de la fouille des joueurs sénégalais a "indigné toute la communauté africaine"
france24fr.description: Une vidéo montrant des joueurs de l'équipe nationale de football sénégalaise se faire fouiller sur le tarmac d’un aéroport américain a massivement été partagée sur les réseaux sociaux. Beaucoup d'internautes se sont insurgés contre un traitement "humiliant". L'équipe du Sénégal a démenti mais la polémique perdure, notamment avec le relais d’intox.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde : les souvenirs les plus marquants des journalistes de France 24
france24fr.description: La Coupe du monde de football 2026 est sur le point de débuter... C'est donc l'occasion parfaite pour se remémorer ses souvenirs les plus marquants en Mondial !

france24fr.title: Mort de Lyhanna : un échec national ?
france24fr.description: Face à l'immense émotion suscitée par la mort de la jeune Lyhanna, 11 ans, dont les obsèques se tiendront vendredi dans l'intimité familiale, le gouvernement français et la justice font l'objet de vives critiques en raison des défaillances présumées de plusieurs institutions, notamment judiciaires. En visite mercredi dans une unité spécialisée de l'hôpital pédiatrique Hôpital Robert-Debré à Paris, E. Macron a estimé qu'il fallait en faire davantage pour "protéger" les enfants des violences.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : NBA, NFL, mode… Le rêve américain des stars du football
france24fr.description: De Buff Donelli à Kylian Mbappé, les footballeurs et les États-Unis entretiennent une histoire d'amour depuis près d’un siècle. Alors que les stars du ballon rond s'affichent dans les salles de la NBA et deviennent ambassadeurs du football américain, le mariage entre ces deux mondes n'a jamais semblé aussi pertinent.

france24fr.title: France : 30 ans de prison pour tentative de meurtre d'un dissident azerbaïdjanais
france24fr.description: Une cour d'assises spéciale à Rennes a condamné mercredi à trente ans de réclusion criminelle Emin Gasimov, considéré comme le "chef" du commando ayant tenté d'assassiner en 2021 à Nantes le blogueur azerbaïdjanais dissident Mahammad Mirzali.

france24fr.title: Darmanin renonce au "plaider-coupable" criminel après le rejet du texte en commission
france24fr.description: Alors que son projet de loi a été rejeté mercredi en commission, le ministre de la Justice Gérald Darmanin, qui fait face aux critiques liées à l'affaire Lyhanna, a annoncé retirer la mesure phare de son texte, le "plaider-coupable" pour les infractions les plus graves.

zeit.title: Anne König: »Frauen müssen nicht von der EU gerettet werden«
zeit.description: Deutschland widersetzt sich der EU-Richtlinie für gerechtere Löhne. Die Frauensprecherin der Union findet das richtig so: Die Wirtschaft müsse vor Schaden bewahrt werden.

zeit.title: Tankrabatt: Tankrabatt endet wie geplant Ende Juni
zeit.description: Die Entlastung beim Tanken wirke, sei finanzpolitisch aber nicht mehr sinnvoll, heißt es aus den Regierungsfraktionen. Der ADAC kritisiert hohe Preisschwankungen.

Porzellan-Pudel: «Bares für Rares»-Star vermacht Mampe seltenes Sammlerstück
Helene Fischer in Dresden: Sie schwebt
zeit.description: Spektakel auf dem Thron, Akrobatik hoch in der Luft, und das Mikrofon ist gülden: Helene Fischer eröffnet ihre »360°«-Tournee. Ja, schön war’s.

zeit.title: Schadenersatz-Forderungen: Hohe Schadenersatzklagen gegen Sparkasse nach Einbruchscoup
Sportwetten: Rote Karten warnen vor Suchtgefahr zur WM
Hailey Bieber: Wie man gut geölt in den Tag startet
zeit.description: Hailey Bieber hat ein neues Ritual für sich entdeckt – und freut sich, dass sie sich damit so richtig schön alt fühlt. Da haben wir den Salat!

zeit.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Anpfiff in Amerika – Drei Gastgeber, viele Konflikte
zeit.description: Die Fußball-Weltmeisterschaft startet. Wie beeinflussen die USA als Gastgeber die politische Stimmung rund um das Turnier? Und: Debatte über Kinderschutz in Frankreich

zeit.title: JD Vance und Marco Rubio: Vance gegen Rubio, wer wird Trumps Nachfolger?
zeit.description: JD Vance und Marco Rubio wollen beide Präsident werden. Wer hat bessere Chancen? In der Livefolge des US-Podcasts diskutieren wir darüber – und beantworten Hörerfragen.

Kameras gegen Falschparker: Busse knipsen Falschparker - Stadt weitet Pilotprojekt aus
Elbvertiefung: Der tägliche Newsletter aus Hamburg: Die neue Köhlbrandbrücke … sieht aus wie die alte Köhlbrandbrücke

nzz.title: In Trub im Emmental ist die 10-Millionen-Schweiz weit weg – aber die Idylle ist bedroht, egal wie am Sonntag abgestimmt wird
nzz.description: Funktioniert das Land auch da, wo es schrumpft? Eine Reportage.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Die Übernahme der Commerzbank ist ein normaler Vorgang. Ihre Blockade ist zwecklos.
nzz.description: Die Schwäche deutscher Banken hat auch politische Gründe. Dass sie zu Übernahmezielen werden, ist da nur konsequent. Auch deshalb sollte sich die Regierung zurückhalten.

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ AKZENT» - USA und Mexiko: eine komplizierte Fussball-Beziehung
nzz.description: Politisch sind die USA und Mexiko zerstritten. Beim Fussball aber sind sie ein Markt – gerade wegen der vielen mexikanischstämmigen Menschen in den USA. Analyse einer komplizierten Partnerschaft.

nzz.title: Die Preise in Amerika steigen immer schneller an: Der Iran-Krieg hinterlässt deutliche Spuren in der US-Wirtschaft
nzz.description: Die Teuerung und der robuste Arbeitsmarkt bescheren dem neuen Chef der amerikanischen Notenbank Probleme. Tiefere Leitzinsen, wie sie Donald Trump verlangt, liegen nicht drin.

nzz.title: Jeffrey Epstein habe ihn erpressen wollen, sagt Bill Gates vor dem Kongressausschuss
nzz.description: Der Philanthrop galt als der am meisten bewunderte Mensch der Welt. Dann wurden erst seine Affären und schliesslich sein enger Draht zu Epstein bekannt. Und nun soll auch sein bescheidenes Auftreten nichts als eine Show sein.

nzz.title: SpaceX wird der grösste Börsengang der Geschichte: Das sind die zehn wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten
nzz.description: Das Raumfahrtunternehmen SpaceX kommt an die Börse und heizt die Euphorie im Technologiesektor an. Anleger hoffen auf Kurssteigerungen, doch der Börsengang hat Risiken.

nzz.title: 10-Millionen-Schweiz: Die Schweiz muss es besser machen als das Ausland
nzz.description: Die Initiative zur Begrenzung der Schweizer Bevölkerung zielt direkt auf die Beziehungen der Schweiz zur EU ab. Doch das ist keine Lösung, wie Erfahrungen aus dem Ausland zeigen.

nzz.title: Zuwanderung und Ständemehr: Das Parlament muss entscheiden, wie ernst es die Verfassung nimmt
nzz.description: Am Donnerstag geht es im Ständerat um zwei Fragen: Muss die Schweiz den Zuwanderungsartikel anpassen, damit sie die EU-Verträge abschliessen darf? Und soll sich das Parlament politischen Spielraum bewahren, indem es die Schubert-Praxis kodifiziert?

nzz.title: «Sind amerikanische Leben mehr wert als unsere?» Eine Stadt in Kenya steht kopf, weil die USA dort ein Ebola-Quarantänezentrum für ihre Bürger bauen
nzz.description: Eigentlich ist Nanyuki ein friedlicher Safari-Ort. Doch nun rollen Armeefahrzeuge durch die Strassen. Und Tränengas verhüllt den Mount Kenya. Ein Augenschein.

nzz.title: Getäuscht mit Gold aus der Schweiz? Ein Finanzskandal in Indien führt nach Luzern und ins Tessin
nzz.description: Valcambi, die grösste Schweizer Goldraffinerie, ist in indischer Hand. Doch der Eigentümer soll ihren Umsatz jahrelang stark frisiert haben und täuschte so Investoren, wie Behörden sagen. Der Trick war simpel.

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ MACHTSPIEL» - Wie wird mit Umfragen Politik gemacht, Thomas Petersen?
nzz.description: Messen Umfragen politische Stimmungen nur oder beeinflussen sie sie? Der Meinungsforscher Thomas Petersen sagt: Der Effekt auf das Wahlverhalten sei minimal bis nicht vorhanden . Aber Demokratien brauchten sie: um aus Ideologiefragen Sachfragen zu machen.

nzz.title: Nationalhelden oder Massenmörder? Ein Streit mit historischem Hintergrund eskaliert zwischen Warschau und Kiew
nzz.description: Präsident Selenski hat eine Militäreinheit nach einer Partisanenarmee benannt, die im Zweiten Weltkrieg Massaker an der polnischen Bevölkerung verübte. Die Empörung in Polen ist riesig. So angespannt war das bilaterale Verhältnis der beiden Staaten noch nie seit Kriegsbeginn.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Das F-Wort zieht immer: Die Linke hat Faschismus zum Kampfbegriff gemacht. Dass damit eine menschenverachtende Ideologie verharmlost wird, nimmt sie in Kauf
nzz.description: Der Faschismusvorwurf hat Konjunktur. Wer «Faschist» sagt, will zeigen, dass er auf der richtigen Seite steht. So unsinnig der Vorwurf auch sein mag, er lässt kaum jemanden kalt.

nzz.title: Künstliche Intelligenz löst ein 80 Jahre altes Mathe-Rätsel. «Problem-Prompting» könnte die Zukunft der Mathematik sein
nzz.description: Stirbt die «schöne Mathematik», wenn Mathematiker aus Silizium das Feld besetzen? Keineswegs. Die KI-Krise ist eine Chance.

nzz.title: Preisen und beten – Mette-Marits kranke Lunge mobilisiert Norwegens Kulturschaffende
nzz.description: Die norwegische Prinzessin zeigt sich nicht mehr ohne Atemhilfe. Inzwischen weiss man, dass eine Lungentransplantation unumgänglich geworden ist. Die Solidarität im Land ist gross, insbesondere und nicht zufällig auch in der Literatur- und Kunstszene.

observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.description: Numa visita longa a diferentes cidades espanholas, Leão XIV foi recebido por multidões e falou em “golaço” da Igreja Católica. Que mensagem passou o Papa? Uma conversa com o Padre João Basto.

observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.description: Comando Sub-Regional do Câvado afirma que não há habitações em perigo. Ainda, Porugal vence Nigéria por 2-1.

observador.title: 2h. Trump. "É o cessar-fogo mais violado da história"
observador.description: Presidente norte americano revela que ataques vão continuar caso não haja memorando de entendimento com Irão. Ainda, Portugal vence Nigéria por 2-1.

observador.title: 1h. Portugal vence Nigéria por 2-1
observador.description: Equipa das Quinas vence dois jogos de preparação para o campeonato do mundo. Ainda, Irão diz que Estreito de Ormuz está "fechado a todos os tipos de embarcações".

observador.title: POR x NIG. "Há esperança nesta equipa!"
observador.description: No último teste antes do Mundial, Gabriel Alves acredita que Martinez "esteve bem na gestão física da equipa", fala de Ronaldo, que "não conseguiu a definição", e de Conceição, que "espalhou brasas."

observador.title: As ideias do Papa
observador.description: Perante uma assembleia política que vai da esquerda radical do Podemos à direita radical do Vox, Leão XIV revelou Fé e sentido de Estado, espiritualidade e realismo

observador.title: O maior espetáculo desde o Big Bang
observador.description: Apesar de termos cara de terraplanistas, nós, os malucos por futebol, sabemos perfeitamente que o mundo é uma bola.

observador.title: O melhor dos fins do mundo possíveis
observador.description: Há um mundo que ainda existe, que ainda se interessa por filosofia, por pintura, pelos cinemas de rua, pela verdade, o que quer que ela seja, por aquilo de que pode ser capaz o engenho humano.

observador.title: POR x NIG. "Golo por validar a favor de Portugal!"
observador.description: "Jogador da Nigéria por expulsar", golo nigeriano nascido de um pontapé de baliza que era canto e golo por marcar a favor de Portugal: "erros graves" que valem ao árbitro "uma nota muito negativa."

observador.title: Uma tradição fora da vidraça
observador.description: Não há maneira de, simultaneamente, preservar as marchas dos Santos Populares e fechar os vestígios delas num museu.

observador.title: 00h. EUA lançam ataques "contra vários alvos" no Irão
observador.description: Pentágono diz ser uma "resposta à agressão injustificada e contínua do Irão". Ainda, a seleção nacional venceu a Nigéria por 2-1.

observador.title: A encruzilhada
observador.description: A janela para uma deliberação significativa sobre segurança está a estreitar-se, e pessoas fora das empresas de IA devem ser envolvidas nessa discussão antes que seja tarde.

observador.title: Chapéus há muitos
observador.description: A APA e a Ministra do Ambiente vêm como defensores dos banhistas, dos chapéus-de-sol e da inveja contra os concessionários - os mesmos que asseguram apoios de praia, vigilância e nadadores-salvadores.

observador.description: Cada vez mais a USF AN e os Sindicatos Médicos se afirmam por “USFs centradas nos Profissionais”. O Lema com que a Reforma se impôs, “USFs centradas nos utentes“, nunca mais se ouviu…

observador.title: "Trabalhamos com jogadores que lutam para estar no onze"
observador.description: Depois do Chile, Portugal venceu a Nigéria antes de rumar aos EUA, numa altura em que Martínez admite ter mais dúvidas do que certezas. Técnico utilizou 26 jogadores nos dois jogos (só faltou Velho).

spiegel.title: Lobbyismus: Wirtschaft steigert EU-Lobbyausgaben um 49 Prozent
spiegel.description: Die Wirtschaft gibt Rekordsummen aus, um die Politik der EU zu beeinflussen – das zeigt eine aktuelle Analyse. An der Spitze stehen US-Techkonzerne wie Amazon und Apple.

spiegel.title: Saunameister werden: Wie man mit nackten Körpern und ätherischen Ölen umgeht
spiegel.description: Früher war er Bankkaufmann, heute wedelt er nackten Gästen heiße Luft zu. Hier erzählt Saunameister Marius Wellmann, wie er mit ätherischen Ölen, schwachen Kreisläufen und zu viel körperlicher Nähe umgeht.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Die neuen Trikots zwischen Arbeitskleidung und Kunst
News: Auftakt der Fußball-WM, Frust in der SPD, EZB entscheidet über Leitzins
spiegel.description: In Mexiko beginnt die Fußball-WM der Herren. In der SPD braut sich Unmut über die Parteispitze zusammen. Und in Frankfurt entscheidet die EZB über den Leitzins. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagmorgen.

spiegel.title: Proteine: Macht uns viel Eiweiß auf Dauer krank?
spiegel.description: Zu viel Eiweiß könnte zu Gesundheitsschäden und mehr Krebserkrankungen führen – das sagt ein renommierter Altersforscher. Übersehen wir eine Gefahr durch Eiweißpulver und High-Protein-Produkte?

spiegel.title: Schnarchen: Was wirklich hilft
spiegel.description: Schnarchen nervt – vor allem die Mitschläfer. Warum schnarchen wir überhaupt? Und kann man den Krawall im Bett stoppen? Das verrät uns ein Professor für Hals-, Nasen- und Ohrenheilkunde.

spiegel.title: USA und Iran überziehen sich mit Angriffen und Dementis
spiegel.description: Tomahawk-Raketen der USA fliegen auf Ziele in Iran, Teheran will Schiffe in der Straße von Hormus beschießen: Die Waffenruhe hält auch in dieser Nacht nicht. Am Morgen erklärte das US-Militär seine Angriffe für beendet.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Polizei schützt Flughafen in Mexiko-Stadt vor protestierenden Lehrern
spiegel.description: In Mexiko-Stadt startet am Donnerstag die Fußball-WM. Gleichzeitig laufen aber auch Demos von radikalen Lehrergewerkschaften. Zuletzt wurde Sprengstoff gefunden. Deshalb läuft jetzt ein Großeinsatz der Polizei.

spiegel.title: Tiroler Alpen: Deutscher überlebt Nacht schwer verletzt im Schnee
spiegel.description: Kälte, Schnee und Nebel: Ein Wanderer aus Ettlingen geht allein in die Tiroler Berge und kehrt nicht mehr zurück. Nach einer großen Suchaktion wird er gefunden. Die Retter sprechen von einem Wunder.

spiegel.title: Oscars: Glenn Close bekommt Ehren-Oscar
spiegel.description: Achtmal war sie nominiert, achtmal ging sie leer aus: Durch die Karriere von Glenn Close zieht sich eine legendäre Oscar-Pechsträhne. Nun hat die Academy ein Einsehen.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: US-Präsident irritiert mit Jubel über hohe Inflation
spiegel.description: Die Inflation in den USA steigt auf den höchsten Wert seit Jahren. Das ist ein massives Problem für Unternehmen und Verbraucher im Land. Aus dem Weißen Haus allerdings kommt eine gänzlich unerwartete Einschätzung der Lage.

spiegel.title: Iran erklärt Straße von Hormus für komplett gesperrt
spiegel.description: Das US-Militär hat in der zweiten Nacht in Folge Attacken auf Iran gestartet. Die Militärführung in Teheran reagierte umgehend: Die Straße von Hormus sei für alle Schiffe geschlossen. Wer versuche, sie zu passieren, werde angegriffen.

spiegel.title: Bundesregierung: Auf Gipfeltreffen sollen weitere Gespräche mit Sozialpartnern folgen
spiegel.description: Mehr als drei Stunden sprachen Bundesregierung und Sozialpartner. Zumindest darüber, dass Reformen nötig sind, sei man sich laut Regierungssprecher Kornelius einig. Eine Gewerkschafterin verließ das Treffen »gut gelaunt«.

spiegel.title: ICE: Donald Trump stattet US-Einwanderungsbehörden mit zusätzlichen 70 Milliarden Dollar aus
spiegel.description: Donald Trump hat den »Secure America Act« unterzeichnet und stellt 70 Milliarden Dollar für Einwanderungsbehörden wie ICE bereit. Damit ist die brutale Abschiebepolitik bis zum Ende seiner Amtszeit finanziert.

spiegel.title: Hugo Boss: Britischer Großaktionär Frasers will Modehersteller übernehmen
spiegel.description: Bisher gehörten der britischen Frasers-Gruppe rund ein Viertel der Boss-Aktien. Jetzt will das Unternehmen die volle Kontrolle und macht den übrigen Aktionären ein Angebot.

spiegel.title: Mario Voigt: »FAZ« löscht Gastbeitrag nach KI-Hinweisen
spiegel.description: Das Portal »Frag den Staat« hat Auffälligkeiten in Texten von Thüringens Ministerpräsident Mario Voigt entdeckt. Weil die Staatskanzlei Fragen auswich, löschte die »FAZ« nun einen Gastbeitrag.

spiegel.title: Noma in Kopenhagen: Weltberühmtes Restaurant will im August wieder öffnen
spiegel.description: Für viele galt das Noma in Kopenhagen als das beste Restaurant der Welt. Im März schloss es, vorher hatte es Gewaltvorwürfe gegen Küchenchef Rédzepi gegeben. Im August öffnet es nun wieder – mit einem neuen Küchenchef.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Rassistische Ausschreitungen in Belfast und Southampton - Sikhs in Angst
spiegel.description: In Southampton fordern Demonstranten Abschiebungen, in Belfast brennen Häuser und Autos: Aus Kritik an einer angeblich zu woken Polizei wird Hass gegen Migranten.

new-sci.title: Iron Age Britons may have removed the brains of the dead

new-sci.title: Frozen squirrel scat preserves ancient DNA from hundreds of species
new-sci.description: A complex ecosystem of woolly mammoths, bison, horses and big cats has been elucidated by studying the faeces of small rodents that probably ate the bigger animals

new-sci.title: The last-ditch plan to save coral reefs from utter destruction
new-sci.description: Bleaching has devastated reefs around the world, raising fears of an irreversible shift. Yet new interventions have revealed that corals can be remarkably resilient if we can give them enough help to recover

new-sci.title: Why we should all take quantum physics extremely personally
new-sci.description: Physics is considered a cold, hard science – but it will transform your life if you view it with a bit more subjectivity, says Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

new-sci.title: A cosmic case of mistaken identity that can only be solved right now
new-sci.description: Brown dwarfs are somewhere between the size of a planet and a star, so how could we have potentially mistaken two of them for distant galaxies? Columnist Chanda Prescod-Weinstein argues that solving this cosmic mix-up is particularly possible now, as galaxy research has never been stronger

new-sci.title: Dinosaur-killing asteroid impact site stayed hot for millions of years
new-sci.description: Drill cores at the impact site of the Chicxulub asteroid show evidence that, alongside widespread destruction, the collision created a vast underground ecosystem filled with hot water that sheltered microbial life

new-sci.title: Unpicking endometriosis reveals how it affects more than the pelvis
new-sci.description: Endometriosis is usually thought of as a gynaecological condition, but a huge study shows it has links with cholesterol levels, inflammation and an altered microbiome

new-sci.title: You don't need to worry about recursive-self-improving AI – yet

new-sci.title: What really happened when ancient humans migrated out of Africa
new-sci.description: The out-of-Africa migration, in which ancient humans went on to inhabit every other continent except Antarctica, may not have been one moment in time, but a long and slow process. Columnist Michael Marshall examines how archaeologists are rethinking this critical part of our history

new-sci.title: What is a ‘normal’ memory slowdown, and when should I worry?

new-sci.title: Wildlife thrives in solar farm built on restored peatland
new-sci.description: A diverse range of bird species has been recorded at a solar park on rewetted peatland in Germany, suggesting that combining energy generation with habitat restoration could benefit biodiversity, the climate and the economy

phys-org.title: Message drift: Why things get taken out of context online and why it matters
phys-org.description: You are scrolling through your feed when a screenshot appears showing a public figure saying something surprising or controversial. Within minutes, it is everywhere. Some are angry, others defend it, memes parody it, and arguments spread across platforms.

phys-org.title: Pathogenic fungus transmitted by domestic cat scratches is present in wild animals
phys-org.description: The fungus that causes sporotrichosis is typically transmitted among cats and results in serious lesions. Recently, it was found in the internal organs of wild animals. The study was published in March in the journal Mycopathologia.

phys-org.title: Researchers develop a new anti-jellyfish floating buoy
phys-org.description: Researchers from the Universitat Politècnica de València (UPV) and the University of Alicante have developed a new anti-jellyfish floating buoy that helps prevent these creatures from reaching the coast, thereby reducing the risk of stings among bathers.

phys-org.title: Virtual future selves improve students' planning and motivation, with gains seen after six months
phys-org.description: Future-oriented thinking is a cornerstone of healthy decision-making, academic success and mental well-being. Yet many people struggle to act in ways that benefit their future selves, often prioritizing immediate rewards over long-term gains. A new study published in the Journal of Medical Internet Research explores how digital interventions can help bridge this gap by strengthening future self-identification.

phys-org.title: Preschoolers whose parents received coaching had fewer conduct problems, higher cognitive skills in middle school
phys-org.description: Children of parents who received coaching and support materials in preschool had fewer conduct problems in middle school and higher levels of academic skills more than seven years later, according to a new study by an interdisciplinary team of Penn State researchers.

phys-org.title: Butter or margarine? A food scientist describes how subtle chemical deviations can affect your baked goods
phys-org.description: My mother loves butter. It is the primary fat I ate growing up. She smeared it on any kind of bread, potatoes, nut rolls or coffeecake. She baked with it exclusively.

phys-org.title: New iron–scandium catalyst extends carbon nanotube growth at high temperatures
phys-org.description: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are among the most promising nanomaterials for future technologies because of their exceptional mechanical strength, electrical conductivity and thermal performance. However, translating these remarkable properties into practical products depends on the ability to efficiently grow long, high-quality CNTs.

phys-org.title: Research examines how corporate workforce messaging shapes recruiting
phys-org.description: When the Securities and Exchange Commission updated Regulation S-K in 2020 to require public companies to disclose more information about human capital in annual filings, the rule was designed primarily with investors in mind. New research from the University of Miami Patti and Allan Herbert Business School suggests that the regulation may also have reshaped how companies compete for talent.

phys-org.title: Where humpbacks gather near Tokyo's remote islands could reshape whale watching and conservation
phys-org.description: Humpback whales are one of the most popular species for whale watching. Since they are active close to the water's surface, groups of whale watchers can often see them breaching and diving during breeding periods. One popular whale watching destination is the Ogasawara Islands—also known as the Bonin Islands—a remote archipelago about 1,000 kilometers south of Tokyo.

phys-org.title: Silver nanoparticles pave the way for precise DNA cutting and joining
phys-org.description: DNA is composed of long chains that act as the blueprint for living organisms. In genetic engineering, scientists cut DNA at specific sites and join the resulting fragments to other DNA sequences, enabling applications such as advanced crop breeding, treatment of genetic diseases, and the generation of animal models for drug discovery.

phys-org.title: Canada's 'AI for All' strategy has ambitious growth targets, but it falls short on workers and the environment
phys-org.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney unveiled Canada's AI for All strategy on June 4, committing more than $2 billion in new spending and targeting $200 billion in additional GDP growth and 250,000 new jobs by 2031.

phys-org.title: Annual global migration has nearly tripled since 2000, reshaping where and how people move
phys-org.description: Global migration has risen sharply from approximately 13 million people per year in 2000 to around 35 million people per year in 2023. This is according to a new dataset on human migration published in Nature by researchers from the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE), IIASA and the University of Hong Kong.

phys-org.title: NASA's CloudCube pioneers miniaturized radar to study clouds, precipitation
phys-org.description: A compact, multifrequency radar built by a team at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory will make it easier to collect information about dynamic cloud systems. Called CloudCube, this new instrument simultaneously probes the atmosphere with three radar signals, spanning 36 to 240 GHz, for optimized sensitivity to a wide range of water droplet and ice particle sizes.

phys-org.title: Global rice production has nearly doubled over 50 years despite climate change
phys-org.description: Global rice production nearly doubled between the 1960s and the 2010s, despite the negative impacts of climate change, according to a new study from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. The study found that management decisions—including expanded irrigation and increased nutrient inputs—played a central role in sustaining rice production and offsetting climate-related losses. phys-org.title: P53's five-hour rhythm may let resonance target gene networks on command
phys-org.description: Can networks of genes be stimulated using resonance? Researchers at the Niels Bohr Institute are investigating whether the protein p53, which activates a range of different genes, can be induced to communicate with the body's cells "on command." Perhaps resonance is the key to stimulating the body toward a new form of self-healing?

phys-org.title: Study shows gains in preschoolers' executive function with additional teacher training
phys-org.description: Research shows that when preschool teachers participate in professional learning workshops and ongoing coaching with experienced early childhood educators, students improve their language and literacy skills, as well as their social-emotional development.

phys-org.title: New methods make tracking individual bird species during migration possible
phys-org.description: Researchers at Cornell Lab of Ornithology, University of Massachusetts and University of Illinois have developed breakthrough methods to track the migration of individual bird species by combining participatory science data with weather radar technology. This advancement addresses a long-standing limitation in migration monitoring: While radar can detect birds in flight, it cannot identify which species are migrating.

phys-org.title: Wheat root compounds suppress soil microbes, helping retain nitrogen and cut emissions
phys-org.description: On a quiet weekend morning in a greenhouse in Aarhus University Flakkebjerg, rows of wheat plants stand with their roots submerged in clear water. There is no soil, no buffer, no automation to take over the work. Every day, weekends and holidays included, postdoctoral researcher Purna Kumar Khatri comes by to check them. He adjusts the pH drop by drop. If he does not, the roots will suffer. And the experiment will fail.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

proj-syn.title: The Enduring Enigma of Economic Growth
proj-syn.description: Developing countries have made enormous progress in many of the factors behind growth, reflected in stronger institutions, rising education levels, higher life expectancy, and increased investment rates. Yet income convergence with advanced economies has been painfully slow—and in most cases absent.

proj-syn.title: Is the US Stock Market Too Big?
proj-syn.description: With China and India having grown so fast as to compensate for the underperformance of their fellow BRICS (Brazil, Russia, and South Africa), the center of gravity in the global economy continues to shift eastward. The question now is whether—and when—equity valuations will reflect this underlying reality.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Bad Vibes
proj-syn.description: A government that abandons structural agendas whenever sentiment turns negative will still be managing sentiment four years later—with nothing to show for it. Brazil’s “vibecession” is a real problem for the current government; but winning the news cycle is not a real solution.

proj-syn.title: Negotiating With the Antichrist
proj-syn.description: Apocalyptic thinking is seeping into the political discourse, with figures like Peter Thiel, Pete Hegseth, and Aleksandr Dugin portraying political differences as struggles between good and evil. When rivals become mortal enemies, the instruments of politics and diplomacy cannot work.

proj-syn.title: Why Is Europe’s Economy Falling Short?
proj-syn.description: For much of the postwar era, European policymakers have prioritized stability and predictability over fostering breakthrough innovation. Today, as the United States and China compete for AI dominance, a stagnant Europe is struggling to regain its place at the technological frontier.

proj-syn.title: Big Tech’s Shadow Market Power
proj-syn.description: Big Tech firms are amassing market power through strategies that bypass current rules for oversight, investigation, and intervention. Unless and until regulators account for the full scope and scale of these strategies, Silicon Valley’s dominance will remain unchallenged.

proj-syn.title: The AI Revolution Mirrors the Green Transition
proj-syn.description: The need for massive upfront investments and the likelihood of significant job displacement imply remarkable parallels between the AI buildout and the green transition. In both cases, the state has an important role to play in guiding market forces on behalf of the public good.

proj-syn.title: Where Is China’s Trillion-Dollar Trade Surplus Going?
proj-syn.description: Whereas China’s trade surplus used to be absorbed largely by the central bank and channeled into official reserves, it is now being redeployed by private actors in search of yield. This indicates China’s progress on financial deepening and underscores markets' increasingly central role in shaping the economy.

proj-syn.title: The Future of Development Finance Is Not Primarily About Money
proj-syn.description: Multilateral development banks have not kept pace with changes to the global financial environment. For middle-income countries like India, accessing knowledge and technology is now a bigger challenge than raising capital, which suggests that these institutions must rethink their operating model.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Perilous French Gambit
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s increasingly close relationship with France marks a departure from six decades of foreign policy aimed at reducing French influence in West Africa. An increasingly close relationship with a power that has long sought to undermine Nigerian influence in West Africa will benefit only politically connected business elites.

proj-syn.title: Autocracy Is Fueling Mexico’s Fiscal Deterioration
proj-syn.description: Mexico’s recent ratings downgrades are merely a symptom of a more serious malady: the ruling Morena party’s efforts to consolidate power permanently. To ensure the legal predictability foreign investors require, President Claudia Sheinbaum would need to confront Morena’s ideological legacy and, more importantly, its cartel ties.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Economy Is Bad News for Republicans
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump triumphed in the 2024 election by continually hammering on the Biden administration’s dismal inflation record. If his party gets shellacked in this year’s midterm elections, it will be because he has made Americans even worse off.

proj-syn.title: SpaceX Is the New East India Company
proj-syn.description: Although SpaceX is not about to rule over foreign subjects, as the chartered companies founded in the early modern era did, it, too, is operating beyond the reach of any sovereign. And like its predecessors, it has already accumulated immense powers that governments will struggle to reclaim.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

proj-syn.title: The Pope and the AI Profiteers
proj-syn.description: In his first encyclical, Pope Leo XIV rightly rejects the idea that markets alone can be trusted to shape society’s technological future. Recognizing that AI raises questions that prices and profits cannot answer, the Chicago-born pope has posed a direct challenge to Chicago School economics.

proj-syn.title: AI Must Not Encroach on Human Dignity
proj-syn.description: In a world captivated by technological advances, Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical seeks to shift attention away from the marvels and terrors of AI and toward the magnificence of humanity. The message that the technology lacks a “moral conscience” and is distinct from human cognition is necessary and welcome.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.
